_rationale.selection_rule: Move the components with the lowest cost per MB saved first: penalty points paid divided by megabytes saved. That is the quantity the greedy and MILP solvers minimise, and it is computed for every component in results/qat/WHY_THESE_COMPONENTS.md. A component is excluded when its cost per MB is one to two orders of magnitude worse than the alternatives.
_rationale.excluded: H0 (10.09% at INT8, 33 cost/MB), H3 (38.15%, 184 cost/MB) and D5 (8.06%, 1712 cost/MB) stay BF16 in every tier. E0, H2, D3, D7 and E5 are also excluded from INT4: at group-32 they cost 41 to 3083 per MB, against 26-31 for E2/E3/E4.
_rationale.why_encoder_blocks: E1-E4 are 2.89M parameters each and hold 11.6 MB of a 54.7 MB model, yet they are the four cheapest rows in the INT8 table (0.14 to 0.46 cost/MB). The cheapest components are also the largest, which is why they carry every tier.
_rationale.entropy_frozen: H0-H3 stay at 16-bit and are frozen during fine-tuning. The bundle ships precomputed integer CDF tables in entropy_control_int.pt; changing those weights would invalidate the bit-exact coding contract.
_rationale.train_scope: backbone = encoder and decoder weights; entropy model and QP controls frozen.
_rationale.tier1: More INT8. Every component whose cost per MB is under roughly 5 goes to INT8; the three intolerant ones stay BF16. This is the aggressive uniform-INT8 hypothesis: 14.4 MB, predicted about 9.1% penalty before any recovery.
_rationale.tier2: Moderate INT4 plus few INT8. The two cheapest INT4 rows (E2 at 26.1 and E3 at 31.4 cost/MB) move to group-32 4-bit, while E1 and E4 stay INT8 because their INT4 cost is 157.5 and 31.2. Tests whether QAT can hold a mixed 4-bit/8-bit encoder.
_rationale.tier3: More INT4. All four encoder blocks at group-32 4-bit: 11.4 MB, predicted hundreds of percent. This is a falsification test, not a candidate. If QAT cannot rescue it, the negative result is the finding and it is reported with numbers.
